title: Why Does My Photo Collage Look Blurry?
description: A collage can look blurry because each photo gets only part of the final image’s pixels.
direct: Open the saved collage before changing its layout. If the saved file is sharp and the shared preview is soft, inspect what the receiving app did to it.
figureAlt: A 3000-pixel-wide three-column collage gives each photo about 1000 pixels before gaps.
figureCaption: AI-generated conceptual illustration, not an App screenshot, measured result or real export. Equal columns get approximately one third of the total width before gaps.
cards.choice.heading: Count pixels per cell
cards.choice.body: In a 3000-pixel-wide image with three equal columns, each cell has about 1000 pixels before borders and gaps. A detailed screenshot in that cell cannot retain the full width of its original.
sections.explain.heading: Separate export from sharing
sections.explain.body: A sharp saved collage can become softer after another app resizes it. Inspect the file in Photos or Files before blaming the layout. Share the exported file directly instead of taking a screenshot of the collage preview. If the saved image is already too small, reduce the number of columns or make separate collages.
sections.practice.heading: What the app can provide
sections.practice.body: Our iPhone app combines 2–30 photos in 11 layouts and saves JPEG or PNG images up to 3000 pixels wide. That is an upper bound, not a promise of 3000 pixels per photo or recovered focus. One export is free; unlimited exports require Pro. For exact format tradeoffs, see the related JPEG/PNG guide.
faqs.reader-question-1.heading: Will PNG rescue text that is already too small in a collage?
faqs.reader-question-1.body: No. PNG can avoid JPEG’s loss during encoding, but it cannot give the individual cell more pixels. Use a wider cell or fewer columns first.
faqs.reader-question-2.heading: What if only one photo looks soft?
faqs.reader-question-2.body: Open its original at a similar scale. If the original is sharp, compare its crop and cell width with the other panels before rebuilding the entire collage.

steps.step-1.text: Import original photos rather than screenshots of previews into Combine Photos: Stitch & Grid.
steps.step-2.text: Choose a layout with enough room for the details that matter. Adjust each image position and zoom while checking the crop.
steps.step-3.text: Export JPEG or PNG, then open the saved file and inspect faces or lettering. Test the destination separately.
